reviewContext.userProblem: Commit 431bfdb exports breadboard boards as Gerber/Excellon ZIPs, but it has no design record and it was not reviewed against board-house upload rules. Silkscreen can print on pads or fall outside the outline, Excellon whole-millimetre coordinates lack a decimal point, the drill header copies another tool's wording, polarity marks can collide with pads, TS/native parity is untested, the test parser is lenient, small circuits cannot be trimmed to a cheaper size tier, and there are no PCB goldens or drift check.

designDecisionsAndRationale: Silkscreen safety is guaranteed by clipping every legend stroke to the legend rectangle and outside per-pad keepout circles (cut, rejoin, filter), with placement that avoids keepouts first; clipping never moves a point, so uncut glyphs such as the 1/6 mm segments of '2' and '5' survive (design 7.1, finding F1).
Square pads use the circumscribed circle for the keepout radius (about 1.5835 mm) for a simple conservative test; round pads use 1.19 mm (design 4).
Polarity marks try five directions (0, +45, -45, +90, -90) and are omitted with a warning rather than clipped, because a clipped '+' could read as '-' (design 7.1 item 4, R5).
Outline mode affects emission only; routing, strips, placement and clipping are computed once in the full-board frame, so 'board' output and copper geometry stay unchanged (design 7.2, 7.6).
Excellon always writes three decimals so METRIC readers never apply zero suppression (R3); the drill header comment is self-authored, keeping the '; #@! TF.FileFunction' convention (R4).
Determinism uses only basic arithmetic and Math.sqrt so Bun (JSC) and Boa produce identical bytes; parity is proven with a native-parity case run by mise run test-cli (design 7.5, R6).
The drift check is a golden test in export-golden.test.ts rather than a CLI --check, which meets the acceptance criterion with less surface (design 7.3).

The validator is an allow-list of exactly what the writer emits and is test-only; the CLI test asserts the written ZIP equals encodeBreadboardPcbZip(exportBreadboardPcb(...)) so core validation covers CLI output (design 7.4).
The 431bfdb byte-diff evidence uses a scratch fixture-export.ts script under tmp/ instead of a git worktree (plan 03 Step 0, review F-PLAN-1).
intentionalTradeoffs: GTO and DRL bytes change versus 431bfdb; GTL, GBL, GTS, GBS and GKO do not (design 7.6).
A reference with no free spot falls back to the first candidate and is partly clipped without a warning (design 7.1 item 3).
The example keeps its e7 two-leads warning and the goldens are generated with it (user QA Q2).
The desktop always exports the full board (user QA Q1).
geometry.ts rotatePoint trigonometry for rotated boards and part outlines is an accepted parity exception; the parity example uses rotation 0.
Accepted residuals: F3 (polarity marks are not checked against label text); L-2 (existing distanceToSegment Math.hypot is used only in routing comparisons).
supportedEdgeCases: Square pin-1 pads (breadboard.ic, breadboard.header) with an R aperture and the circumscribed keepout.
Jumper fallback lines clipped around every pad they cross (c1-c5 fixture).
Parts on the top rail whose four reference candidates are all blocked (R2 fixture).
Full-board holes at x = 127 mm written as X127.000 (R3 fixture).
LED anode with used neighbours in all five mark directions (R5 warning, no mark).
Zero-length segments and tangent keepouts in clipping and in the validator's distance checks.
Rotated boards give identical files in both outline modes.
Board labels partly outside the trimmed outline are dropped whole in used mode.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Checking polarity marks against label text (F3).
Keepout shapes other than circles and general polygon clipping.
Arcs, AM/SR/LPC Gerber commands and inch units in the validator.
Bit-exact parity for rotated boards with non-zero rotation (rotatePoint trigonometry).
Used-mode goldens and a ZIP golden.
